What makes the gap interesting is that Elo cannot break the tie — both men read 2011, a differential of one point across twelve division fights for Hernandez and fourteen for Rodrigues. Two fighters, the same rating, and a sixteen-point disagreement between the model's two engines about what the profiles mean. Both carry full trust, so none of it is a sample-size artifact.

The separator is Hernandez's grappling composite, which reads +2.92 — the highest single composite on this card in any category. It is built from real volume rather than reputation: 0.392 takedowns landed per minute against Rodrigues's 0.126, a control differential of +0.407 against +0.115, 0.109 submission attempts per minute against 0.025, and a raw submission finish rate of 0.556. Rodrigues's counter is that his wrestling defense reads +1.06 to Hernandez's +0.55 and his takedown defense 75.0% to 68.2% — he is not a soft target on the mat, which is why the model still gives him 24.2%.

The striking numbers point the other way and the method split resolves them in a way worth explaining. Rodrigues owns the power composite (+1.17 to -0.02) and the larger hand-tuned knockout-threat index (+1.67 to +1.43), yet a HERNANDEZ knockout is the single largest terminal state at 38.1%, against a Rodrigues knockout at 20.8%. Against Hernandez: he is coming off a round-three knockout loss to Sean Strickland in February, his momentum reads -0.113 against Rodrigues's +0.755, and Rodrigues is 3-0 in his last three with two first-round knockouts.

Read the WC-only setting before anything else here, because it is worth seven points and it lands entirely on one man. De Ridder's edge is the submission, and it is the largest share of his 66.4%: a 23.7% submission against a 29.5% decision and only a 13.3% knockout. Dolidze's own path runs through durability and power: his chin reads +0.55 to de Ridder's -0.20, his chin-damage factor 0.919 to 0.791, his getting-finished index 0.200 to 0.500, and his raw knockout finish rate is 0.667, which funds his 20.1% knockout against de Ridder's 13.3%. Age is the thumb on the scale — Dolidze is 38.1 with an age factor of 0.847 against 35.9 and 0.903 — and neither man is busy, de Ridder's 2.472 volume being the lowest on the card, which is why 40.7% of sims reach the judges and the O/U GBM pushes Over 2.5 up to 61.9% from the simulation's own 54.1%.

The fight moved TOWARD Judice, from 60.4% to 65.3%, which is the opposite of what those two results suggest. The explanation is trust. Judice went from four observed fights to five and from 0.617 trust to 0.831, and the extra fifteen minutes sharpened her power composite from +1.23 to +1.42. Chaves went from one fight to two and 0.214 to 0.429 — and what the new evidence showed was an ordinary three-round decision, so her chin fell from +0.08 to -0.24 and her power from -0.02 to -0.11. Adding evidence about an average fighter makes them look average faster.

That still leaves this as a fight between a measured profile and a partial prior. Chaves is 8-0 as a professional and the model does not dispute it — her pre-UFC record reads eight fights at a 0.875 win rate — but at 0.429 trust roughly half her composite profile is still the divisional average, and it shows: power -0.11, chin -0.24, output +0.16, wrestling defense +0.07. The engines remain far apart, with the hand-tuned model at 87.1% for Judice against the GBM's 72.8%, and the ratings only mildly supporting it at 1642 across five fights to 1576 across two.

Her output composite reads +1.42 and her power +1.42, off a volume of 9.318 — the highest on this card — with a raw knockout finish rate of 0.667 and a +1.63 knockout-threat index against Chaves's -0.22. That gives her a +1.54 decision edge and makes a Judice decision the modal outcome at 44.7%, with a 17.0% knockout behind it, in a fight the model expects to spend 87.8% of its time standing. Chaves's own best path is the submission at 11.0%, which is worth naming for what it is: she has no career submission wins at all and a finishing ability index of 0.000, so that share is the divisional grappling prior showing through Judice's weak mat numbers, not a demonstrated threat.

matchupAnalysis: Lerryan Douglas 65.8% / Jamall Emmers 34.2%, and no fight on this card depends more completely on a single setting. Douglas has two fights totalling 4.15 minutes of cage time — both first-round knockouts, of Julian Erosa in March and Cam Teague on the Contender Series last September — which gives him a computed trust of 0.059. At that value his profile is essentially the featherweight average and the fight reads Emmers 56.1%. The override sets him to 0.600 and the projection inverts: Douglas 65.8%. The full ladder on today's data is Douglas 43.9% at computed trust, 56.8% at 0.450, 65.8% at 0.600 — the favorite flips somewhere around 0.30 and then keeps extending. The override is not an adjustment to this projection; it IS this projection.

What the extra weight lets through is a genuinely extreme set of rates. At 0.600 trust Douglas's power composite reads +2.44 — the highest on the card — with an output of +1.99, an early-finish score of 0.931 (also the card's highest), a finishing ability of 1.000 and a raw knockout finish rate of 1.000, off a volume of 8.675 and a strike differential of +3.855 that is likewise the card's best. The result is a knockout-threat index of +2.88 against Emmers's +0.22, by far the widest gap here, and a Douglas knockout at 31.2% — the modal terminal state in the fight. The honest framing is that these are the rates of a man who has spent four minutes in the Octagon and finished both times inside a round; 0.600 trust says take them at three-fifths weight, and at that weight he is a solid favorite. It is worth adding that his record outside the UFC is much less emphatic — nineteen prior fights at a 0.684 win rate — so the profile the model is extrapolating is the recent form, not the career.

Emmers is the more complete profile and the one the fight length favors. He owns the decision edge (+0.16, though barely), the reach (+1.50, 187.96cm to 182.88cm), the grappling (+0.86 to -0.10), the wrestling defense (+0.85 to +0.25) and 81.3% takedown defense against a man who has never attempted a takedown in the UFC. A Douglas decision (29.2%) and an Emmers decision (22.3%) are the second and third largest buckets, and 51.5% of sims reach the judges. What undermines Emmers is durability and mileage: his chin reads -0.66 with a chin-damage factor of 0.679, his getting-finished index is 0.600, he is 37.1 years old with an age factor of 0.872, and he arrives on a 282-day layoff. He has been knocked out in round one before, by Nate Landwehr in 2024, which is precisely the terminal state Douglas specialises in. Note that the published Over 2.5 of 52.5% is not the naive blend — the coherence guardrail lifted it from 45.6% to clear the fight's 51.5% decision rate, the largest such correction on this card.

One caveat to carry: thirteen of those seventeen fights are at light heavyweight, but every composite is z-scored against the HEAVYWEIGHT population, so his +2.30 reach and his rate stats are being read against a division he has only fought in four times.

This is still the most violent projection on the card. Nzechukwu's knockout-threat index is +2.16 against Gaziev's -0.15, and a Nzechukwu knockout at 42.3% is the single largest terminal state anywhere on this event. His reach composite of +2.30 corresponds to 210.82cm, the longest on the card by a distance, and his career finish profile supports it: a 0.700 knockout finish rate and a 0.800 finishing ability across ten wins, including consecutive first-round knockouts of Chris Barnett and Lukasz Brzeski in his first two heavyweight outings. Only 31.9% of sims reach the judges and 43.9% end in round one, both card extremes, which puts Over 1.5 at 52.5% and Over 2.5 at 38.8% — the shortest projected fight on the card and the only one whose top line sits well below even money.

Gaziev's problem is a -1.72 chin composite, the worst of any man on this card, with a chin-damage factor of 0.535, an early-vulnerability of 0.666 and a getting-finished index of 1.000 — every loss in his sample is a stoppage, including knockouts by Brando Pericic in May and Waldo Cortes Acosta last November. His output composite reads -1.15 and his strike differential -1.987, both card-worst, and his momentum of -0.639 is the lowest here as well. He does hold the higher divisional Elo (1636 to 1575) and a real path: his grappling reads +0.44 to Nzechukwu's -0.25, his wrestling defense +0.87 to +0.37, his control differential +0.383, and his takedown defense 83.3% — and Nzechukwu was submitted in round one by Valter Walker in July 2025 and then lost a decision to Marcus Buchecha in December, so he arrives 0-2. That grappling route is why Gaziev's submission share is 9.7% against a knockout share of 13.8%; under the previous WC-only reading his submission share actually exceeded his knockout share, and the wider sample has narrowed but not erased the point.

synopsis.body: A Nzechukwu KO/TKO at 42.3% is the largest single terminal state on the entire card, off a +2.16 knockout-threat index, a +2.30 reach composite corresponding to 210.82cm, and a 0.700 knockout finish rate. Shortest projected fight here: 43.9% of sims end in round one, only 31.9% reach the judges, Over 1.5 at 52.5% and Over 2.5 at 38.8%. Moderate confidence. Run all-fights with no override — worth -3.7 points against the WC-only reading (70.8%), because opening his sample to thirteen light-heavyweight bouts makes his composites worse across the board while replacing asserted trust with 150 earned minutes. Carry the caveat that those composites are z-scored against the heavyweight population he has fought in only four times, and that he arrives 0-2. Gaziev holds the higher divisional Elo (1636 to 1575) and a real route in his +0.44 grappling, +0.87 wrestling defense and 83.3% takedown defense against a man Valter Walker submitted in round one. What sinks him is a -1.72 chin — the worst of any man here — a 1.000 getting-finished index and two knockout losses in his last three.

matchupAnalysis: Chris Padilla 69.4% / Nasrat Haqparast 30.6%, with the GBM at 28.6% for Haqparast and the hand-tuned model at 15.5%. Padilla also carries the higher divisional Elo, 1830 across five fights to Haqparast's 1776 across fifteen — one of the few fights on this card where the rating and the projection agree against the more experienced man. The trust asymmetry runs the other way, though: Haqparast is at 1.000 on 176 minutes, Padilla at 0.761 on 53.3, so Padilla's advantage is being reported at about three-quarters strength and would widen if you believed his sample outright.

At 95.0% standing time this is the most striking-dominant fight on the card, and Padilla wins that exchange on the model's numbers. His output composite reads +1.04 to Haqparast's +0.49, his reach +1.25 to +0.23 (187.96cm to 182.88cm), his chin +0.45 to -0.85, and his wrestling defense +0.80. Underneath, he lands 47.0% of his head strikes to Haqparast's 40.2% and absorbs 3.003 per minute against a Haqparast figure of 4.057 — the highest absorption rate of any man on this card. That yields a +1.04 knockout-threat index against Haqparast's -0.20, a -0.81 decision edge, and a Padilla decision as the modal outcome at 38.3% with a 21.7% knockout behind it.

The durability comparison is the fight in miniature. Padilla's chin-damage factor is 0.991, his early-vulnerability 0.083 and his getting-finished index 0.000 — he has never been stopped, and three of his four wins are finishes. Haqparast reads 0.740, 0.533 and 0.400, and his most recent outing was a first-round knockout loss to Quillan Salkilld last October, after which he has been out 296 days. What Haqparast retains is real: his wrestling defense composite is the better of the two at +1.21, his takedown defense 86.0%, his effective decision rate 0.727 and his r3-vs-r1 ratio 2.159 — he is a late-rounds fighter who has gone the distance repeatedly, which is what his 18.7% decision share encodes, and 57.0% of sims do reach the judges. Padilla's flags are that his sample is five fights, that his last outing was a majority draw with MarQuel Mederos — who fights earlier on this card as a 22.4% underdog — and that a 0.761 trust means a quarter of his profile is still divisional average.

synopsis.body: Modal outcome is a Padilla decision at 38.3% with a 21.7% knockout; 57.0% of sims reach the judges and 95.0% of fight time is standing — the card's most striking-dominant matchup. He leads on output (+1.04 to +0.49), reach (+1.25 to +0.23) and chin (+0.45 to -0.85), and absorbs 3.003 head strikes per minute against Haqparast's 4.057, the highest of any man here. matchupAnalysis: Jackson McVey 69.0% / Wes Schultz 31.0%, with the GBM at 70.6% and the hand-tuned model at 57.9%, and the ratings marginally supporting it at 1547 to 1502. This is the least-constrained fight on the card by a clear margin: McVey's computed trust is 0.178 — the lowest of the twenty fighters here — on three fights and 12.45 minutes, and Schultz's is 0.359 on four fights and 25.1 minutes. Roughly four-fifths of McVey's composite profile is the middleweight average, so almost nothing below should be read as a strong claim about either man.

What separates them in the model is durability against a striking profile. McVey's chin reads +0.18 with a chin-damage factor of 1.000 against Schultz's -1.02 and 0.750, and Schultz's early-vulnerability of 0.810 is the highest on the card. McVey also leads on reach (+1.00 to +0.75), output (+0.52 to -0.04) and the underlying striking rates by a wide margin: 63.5% head-strike accuracy — the best on this card — against 34.7%, a volume of 6.506 against 2.908, and a strike differential of +3.133 against -0.199. That produces a +1.18 knockout-threat index against Schultz's -0.22 and a McVey knockout at 32.4%, the modal outcome, with 37.1% of all sims ending in round one.

The honest reading of both records complicates that badly, and it is the most interesting thing about this fight. NEITHER MAN HAS A KNOCKOUT WIN — both read 0.000 on knockout finish rate — and yet the model's modal outcome is a knockout. Every one of McVey's three fights has ended in a submission: he submitted Sedriques Dumas in round one in April, and was submitted by Zach Reese and by Brunno Ferreira before that, so his finishing ability and getting-finished indices both read 1.000 and his takedown defense is 0.0%. Schultz is the mirror image: both of his wins are submissions, he attempts 0.239 submissions per minute (the highest rate on the card), and his own takedown defense is also 0.0%. So the model's 13.6% Schultz submission share is his single best path and is probably the most under-stated number in this fight — two fighters who have never stopped a takedown, one of whom hunts submissions and one of whom has been submitted twice in three outings. The published Over 2.5 of 39.9% is post-guardrail, lifted from a naive 35.0% to clear the 39.9% decision rate.

synopsis.body: Modal terminal state is a McVey KO/TKO at 32.4%, off a +1.18 knockout-threat index, the card's best head-strike accuracy (63.5% to 34.7%) and a +3.133 strike differential; 37.1% of sims end in round one. Schultz's -1.02 chin and card-high 0.810 early-vulnerability are the target. Lowest confidence on the card. McVey's computed trust is 0.178 — the lowest of these twenty fighters — on three fights and 12.45 minutes, so four-fifths of his profile is divisional average. And the shape is probably wrong even if the direction is right: NEITHER man has a knockout win (both 0.000 KO finish rate), yet a knockout is the modal projection. All three of McVey's fights ended in submission (he lost two of them that way), both of Schultz's wins are submissions, Schultz attempts the most submissions per minute on the card, and BOTH men have 0.0% takedown defense. Schultz's 13.6% submission share looks like the most under-priced number here.

The caveat is the familiar one: Dyer's computed trust is 0.304 on two fights and 21.3 minutes, so most of her composite profile is the strawweight average, while Reed sits at full trust on 97.6 minutes. The number is built far more on what Reed has been measured doing than on what Dyer has demonstrated.

Reed's profile is the most comprehensively negative on the card. Her chin reads -1.81 — the worst here — with a chin-damage factor of 0.613 and a getting-finished index of 1.000; her grappling is -1.06 and her wrestling defense -0.99, with a control differential of -0.334 and 53.1% takedown defense; her reach composite is -0.37, corresponding to 160.02cm, the shortest on the card; her raw finish rate is 0.000, meaning no stoppage wins in her UFC career at all, against a finishing ability index of 0.000. She is 33.7 years old, her momentum reads -0.452 and her recent-three win rate 0.333, and she arrives on a 457-day layoff — the longest of anyone here — after a round-two knockout loss to Denise Gomes in May 2025. Against that, Dyer's +2.27 knockout-threat index and 1.000 chin-damage factor produce a 51.1% Dyer decision as the modal outcome, with a 17.5% knockout and a 15.1% submission behind it.

Two things deserve to sit alongside the 83.7%. The first is that Reed's own knockout-threat index reads +1.36 — not a small number — because Dyer's chin composite is -1.32 and Dyer absorbs 3.148 head strikes per minute. Reed has one live route, and the model's 3.4% knockout share arguably understates it more than any other number in this fight. The second is that Dyer's measured record is 1-1: a round-two knockout of Ravena Oliveira in March against a Contender Series decision loss to Carol Foro. Her volume of 7.706 and 100% takedown defense are real and encouraging, and at 25.3 she is eight years younger with the better age factor, but two fights is two fights and her own head-strike accuracy is only 33.9%. Expect a long fight either way — 61.0% of sims reach the judges, and the published Over 2.5 of 62.9% is post-guardrail, lifted from a naive 58.6% to clear that decision rate.

synopsis.body: Modal outcome is a Dyer decision at 51.1% with a 17.5% knockout and 15.1% submission behind it; 61.0% of sims reach the judges. The margin is built on Reed's measured decline — a card-worst -1.81 chin, a 1.000 getting-finished index, -1.06 grappling, -0.99 wrestling defense, a 0.000 career finish rate, a 457-day layoff (the longest here) and a knockout loss to Denise Gomes last time out. Moderate confidence at most despite the size of the number. Dyer is at 0.304 trust on two fights and 21.3 minutes, so this is a verdict on Reed rather than a demonstration by Dyer, her own record is 1-1, and her head-strike accuracy is only 33.9%. Note Reed's knockout-threat index still reads +1.36 against Dyer's -1.32 chin and 3.148 absorption rate — her 3.4% KO share is the number most likely to be understated.
